facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has replaced 90% of the assets stolen in a record $6.3 billion hack by using its own funds to purchase replacement tokens, the company said on Saturday.
facts.text: Binance has replaced 90 percent of the assets stolen in a record hack by purchasing replacement tokens using its own company reserves.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has replaced 90% of the assets stolen in a record $6.3 billion hack by using its own funds to purchase replacement tokens, the company said on Saturday.
facts.text: The security breach resulted in the theft of 6.3 billion dollars in digital assets from Binance.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: The company added that it had internally allocated around $6.34 billion from its own funds to cover the losses.
facts.text: Binance internally earmarked 6.34 billion dollars from its own funds to cover customer losses from the cyberattack.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: The remaining 10% comprises less liquid tokens, which could take longer to acquire, Binance said in a statement posted on X.
facts.text: The remaining 10 percent of stolen cryptocurrency consists of less liquid tokens that require additional time to procure.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: The money spent re-buying tokens came from using part of its $1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some of its Futures insurance fund, and the company's own corporate treasury, it said on X.
facts.text: Binance funded the token repurchases in part by drawing on its 1 billion dollar Secure Asset Fund for Users emergency reserve.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: The company wrote on its X account that the estimated total impact sat at around $6.3 billion. It said it has worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with roughly $3 billion frozen on-chain so far.
facts.text: Binance coordinated with blockchain network partners to freeze approximately 3 billion dollars worth of the stolen crypto assets on-chain.

facts.label: reported
facts.text: Cryptocurrency prices declined on Friday as Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, sought to reassure customers that their funds remained safe following the theft of more than $6 billion worth of digital assets.
